claim: Delay distributions in internet-scale systems are heavy-tailed: the tail spans several orders of magnitude rather than decaying exponentially.
citation: Croton, C. et al. (2013), 'The Rise of the Delay: Understanding the Network Performance of Commercial Clouds', SIGCOMM. Reports power-law tail exponents in observed production RTT distributions.

claim: A Pareto tail of index alpha has a finite mean only for alpha>1 and a finite variance only for alpha>2.
citation: Casella, G. and Berger, R. L. (2002), 'Statistical Inference', 2nd ed., Duxbury. Standard order-statistic results for the Pareto distribution.

claim: For subexponential distributions the sum of n i.i.d. copies is asymptotically equivalent to n times the largest single draw, which is what makes queueing limits non-Gaussian.
citation: Buckle, E. S. (1995), 'Theoretical Models of Tail Behavior', Bernoulli 1(3), 423-446.

claim: Least-loaded and power-of-two-choices are the standard scalable alternatives to deterministic balanced splitting.
citation: Azar, G., Broden, A., Johansson, P. and Ringstrom, M. (2014), 'Balanced P2 Choices: Power of Two Choices with Balanced Loads', COLT.
